title: Symmetry Constrained Quantum Error Mitigation for the Schwinger Model
authors: Alexander Tomlinson, Graham Van Goffrier, Bipasha Chakraborty, Zhenyu Cai
abstract: Quantum error mitigation (QEM) is at the very heart of near-term quantum simulations and lattice gauge theories are no exceptions, rather their physical symmetries provide natural consistency checks on noise quantum states. In this work, we exploit the parity and fermion-number symmetries of a gauge theory, the (1+1)-dimensional Schwinger model, under depolarising noise and investigate symmetry verification under digital quantum simulation. We investigate two set-ups - symmetry- sector post-selection in adiabatic state preparation followed by real-time measurements of the chiral condensate and symmetry verification within a variational quantum eigensolver (VQE). In the first case, post-selection reduces the bias in the chiral condensate consistently removing up to 60% of the quantum noise induced error in our system. Motivated by the observed regularity of the residual bias (in the low-noise regime), we further introduce a global-noise calibration obtained from classically accessible smaller lattices and implemented on larger lattices recovering noiseless chiral condensate values within statistical uncertainty. However, in VQE, symmetry verification does not seem to generally improve the optimised parameters or the fidelity of the prepared states, although it reduces the bias in the estimated ground-state energy. This demonstates that improving a noisy cost-function estimator in variational algorithms does not necessarily improve the outcome of the algorithm. Our results show the strength of symmetry verification in different approaches while establishing that its usefulness critically depends on where it is applied in the computational workflow, and provide practical guidance for symmetry-assisted quantum error mitigation in quantum simulations of lattice gauge theories.
summary: This work investigates using inherent physical symmetries to mitigate noise in quantum simulations of the Schwinger model. By comparing post-selection during adiabatic evolution with symmetry checks during VQE, the authors demonstrate that symmetry constraints are highly effective for bias reduction in certain workflows. The findings provide practical guidelines for applying symmetry-assisted QEM in lattice gauge theory simulations.
main_problem: The paper addresses the challenge of Quantum Error Mitigation (QEM) in near-term quantum simulations of lattice gauge theories.
main_result: Symmetry verification is a powerful tool for bias reduction, particularly in adiabatic state preparation, but its utility in variational algorithms is context-dependent.
method: The authors compare post-selection (for adiabatic preparation) against in-the-loop symmetry verification (for VQE) to mitigate noise effects.
model_or_system: The primary model is the (1+1)-dimensional Schwinger model, a U(1) lattice gauge theory, whose symmetries (parity and fermion-number) are exploited for error checking.
key_observables: Chiral condensate expectation value and ground-state energy.
important_parameters: Noise probability ($p$), lattice size ($N$), and the critical noise level ($p^*$).
main_assumptions: The usefulness of symmetry verification critically depends on where it is applied within the overall quantum computational workflow (e.g., post-selection vs. VQE optimization).
figures_summary: Figures compare the performance of various mitigation strategies (e.g., symmetric mitigation vs. global noise correction) on observables like the chiral condensate, showing the effectiveness of post-selection in adiabatic dynamics.
paper_structure: The paper first introduces the physical problem and the Schwinger model Hamiltonian. It then details and compares two main mitigation approaches: symmetry-sector post-selection in adiabatic state preparation, and symmetry verification within the VQE framework. Finally, it presents results showing the differential success of these methods.
why_interesting: The explicit comparison of mitigation techniques (post-selection vs. VQE-based) provides practical guidance on how to integrate physical symmetries into near-term quantum algorithms, which is highly relevant for developing robust quantum simulation protocols.
